Founders lose investors in the first few mins of a pitch. Not because the tech isn't good. Often because they start with features, instead of the problem they're solving. That's the topic on this week's Sound Investments podcast. Dana Sather Robinson has watched this happen for a decade. As founder of Pitch4Impact, she's coached hundreds of tech founders who had transformative technology but couldn't get investors to understand why it mattered. The mistake? Diving into what you're building before establishing: → Why it matters → Who will buy it → How big the opportunity is Here's what we discuss: The pitch isn't just about fundraising. It's a signal of leadership ability. Can the founder recruit talent? Close customers? Inspire belief? VCs screen for this. Weak communication = red flag. But communication is learnable. This week on Sound Investments, Dana breaks down: - Why "PowerPoint poisoning" kills your pitch - How Q&A reveals whether you understand your business - Why eighth-grade language works for even sophisticated investors 🎧 Episode: https://pod.fo/e/37821f 📻 Sub: https://lnkd.in/g6k-nfaA 📝 Deep dive: https://lnkd.in/ggNNi3dA 28 4 Comments Chris Erwin RockWater Industries LLC • 12K followers A podcast event biz "merged" w/ the industry's largest trade org 5 things stand out about the deal 👇 • Both co's were bootstrapped • Both were founder owned & controlled • Combined ownership is 50/50 going forward • Combines events + trade org biz models • Rides momentum of premium B2B Have you heard about it? If not, it's a good one to read about. The 2 companies are 𝗣𝗼𝗱𝗰𝗮𝘀𝘁 𝗠𝗼𝘃𝗲𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁 and 𝗦𝗼𝘂𝗻𝗱𝘀 𝗣𝗿𝗼𝗳𝗶𝘁𝗮𝗯𝗹𝗲. We did a deep dive on the deal in last week's M&A newsletter. Read it here: https://lnkd.in/eSDNZ5tQ -- I'm the founder of RockWater Industries. We do M&A and strategy advisory for creator eocnomy and digital / audio agencies. 6 Mojtaba Asadian, MBA IOPn • 10K followers The future founder won’t pitch investors, they’ll have to prove value to a community. That’s the beauty of fractional and community-led ownership - made possible in Web3. New models of business and ownership are emerging on the back of this, and they prioritize community value creation over capital valuation. Through systems like tokenized economies, founders are building with their users. They are designing ecosystems where the same people who believe in their product are also those who are funding it and growing it. Value-led capital creation is different from capital that comes from a term sheet. This paradigm shift is building more than just companies. It’s building economies and societies. #Web3 #Innovation #Business 13 2 Comments Daren Smith Craftsman Films • 12K followers Most creative investors don’t realize they’re still on the hook after the wire clears. The check is just the beginning. This week’s newsletter breaks down what happens after you invest in a film: • Why staying engaged protects your return • How distribution and marketing are often won through relationships, not ads • What the 15–36 month film timeline really looks like It’s a clear, honest look behind the curtain of indie filmmaking, and a practical guide to being the kind of Executive Producer creatives fight to work with again. If you missed it, the full essay is live now: https://lnkd.in/gj994jh6 17 5 Comments GS Periwal Seed VC Innovation Limited • 3K followers Capital is fuel. But fuel without ignition? 🔥 It just burns out. At Seed VC, we’ve learned ignition comes from three things: 1️⃣ Products & services proven by real customers 2️⃣ Founders who bootstrap through tough days 3️⃣ A strategy that accelerates growth with discipline This is why we say: 👉 Fund strategy > fund size. 👉 True partnership > passive capital. Because in the end, it’s not the fuel alone that drives the journey. It’s the spark + driver + map that make the ride worth it. 💭 For the founders and investors here: what do you think drives success more — fund size or fund strategy? 21 2 Comments Jonah Blake LiveFrameAI • 7K followers I think Phantom Magic Eden MetaMask etc could be leaving eventually billions of dollars on the table not adding video features. No one has disrupted the media model in a way like YouTube and Twitch and that was about 20 years ago. Here’s what I would do if I was a crypto wallet co: 1. Create some form of new tagging and metadata system around cashtags. 2. Allow users to submit a video under a searchable token. There is ai and moderator tools for each upload. So for example $MLG coin will not only have the token but below a list of videos associated by that tag. Make it short form vertical. 3. Create a video FYP and turn cashtags into a real searchable function. I have other ideas on how to do this, but eventually a crypto wallet business will be as profitable as running an exchange. 18 1 Comment Ivan Branitskiy ADI Foundation • 4K followers What happens to stablecoin yields if interest rates collapse? Spoiler: they don’t lose their edge. Let’s walk through this: We know ZIRP was a policy misstep. It inflated speculative bubbles, widened inequality, and delivered little in real growth. No serious macro voice expects a return to zero. We're in an era where the cost of capital is structurally higher. Even so, let’s hypothetically drop rates to zero. Would stablecoins become irrelevant? Not at all. Yield is only part of the equation. The real advantages are functional: - Instant settlement - Global coverage - 24/7 uptime - Composability across DeFi and fintech ecosystems But the biggest shift is in eliminating the “float” - the days when banks hold your money, earn interest, and you wait. Payrolls, social benefits, rent, B2B invoices; trillions cycle through those delays every year. Stablecoins collapse that window. They return yield and agency back to users, not to intermediaries. So no, this isn’t just about chasing 4% yields. It’s about recapturing economic value, rewriting rails, and letting money move freely again. #stablecoins #payments #banks #crypto https://lnkd.in/ghAniRGP 5 Lisa Piercey Oakworth Capital Bank • 4K followers Buying a business? You'll need to bring equity to the table, usually around 40-70% of the enterprise value. Here's where to get it: 1. Personal Capital 2. Friends & Family 3. Angel Investors 4. Family Offices 5. Independent Sponsors 6. Private Equity Funds 7. Search Fund Investors 8. Strategic Partners 9. Seller Equity / Rollover 10. Private Credit Lenders Each source brings its own priorities and expectations, and the best buyers use those differences to build strong partnerships, not just capital stacks. Check out the Resources page on my website for an investor pitch deck checklist and more: https://lnkd.in/e6qC2ttc 23 Paul Hsu Decasonic • 14K followers A Harsh Truth: consumer products that lead with tech are killing their adoption. Founders are racing to build with crypto and AI, as they should. These are generational platforms that open up entirely new design spaces. But here’s the part no one wants to say out loud: The more you emphasize your technology, the more consumers tune out. That language? It’s for founders. It’s for investors. It’s not how mainstream consumers think. It’s not what mainstream consumers crave, desire or aspire. Mainstream users don’t care that your product is decentralized, model-optimized, or cryptographically secure. They care that it works instantly. That it feels intuitive. That it gives them something valuable without effort or confusion. If AI helps me get to a better outcome 10x faster and smarter, I’ll use it again. If crypto infra gives me ownership, portability, or financial upside without me needing to understand how, I’ll stay. But the second you force me to engage with the tech itself, you’ve lost me. The tech stack isn’t the product. It’s the enabler. The best experiences make it invisible. The brands that win will be the ones that translate advanced capabilities into emotionally resonant outcomes: - “Your trip, booked in 30 seconds.” - “Rewards that move with you.” - “A coach that knows you better than your best friend.” No mention of AI. No mention of crypto. Just magic. So yes, build with the most advanced models. Go onchain. But don’t expect consumers to clap for your architecture. They’ll clap when it feels like the future. Not when you tell them it is. 19 1 Comment Harry Groome Melt Ice Cubes • 4K followers As we are days away from launching Melt in Florida and online in 45 states, we’ve learned just how complex it is to build a Shopify-compliant checkout for hemp-derived TH🌊 beverages. Shopify doesn’t allow TH🌊 brands to use its built-in payment system — and it still charges platform fees. So, we partnered with an approved vendor, Bankful, which specializes in compliant processing for high-risk categories. Approval takes time and paperwork - a few weeks and about 6–8% total in transaction costs between Shopify and Bankful. Age gates and shipping rules aren’t automatic. Every state restriction must be built manually, and each compliance app adds monthly cost and complexity. Testing takes longer than building. Every flow — cart, checkout, email, and order alert — needs to be perfect before launch. Bottom line: A third-party cart setup runs about $500–$650 upfront and $100–$150/month ongoing. A bit of a hassle — but worth it for a compliant, age-gated, and reliable checkout experience. If you’re building in this space let me know what else to look out for. #Shopify #Bankful #THCBeverages #Ecommerce #DTC #MeltCubes 20 3 Comments Aleks Zedmin Hashtek • 1K followers Is legacy-level quality possible in a regulated market? In this conversation with Chas & Kevin, founders of 1 Above, we discuss transparency, scaling without sacrificing standards, and why cutting corners on inputs always catches up with you. One point that stood out: “It was better when it was illegal.” Not because regulation is bad — but because standards were personal. Their lab is powered by the Hashtek A-Series, built for consistent, high-torque, low-speed agitation designed to mimic hand washing while maintaining repeatability at scale. Full episode premieres tonight at 7 PM EST. You can explore all of our videos here: https://hashtek.ca/video/ Subscribe to the YouTube channel here: https://lnkd.in/gGxrs_E3 If you’re building in this space, I’d be curious: What’s the biggest challenge in maintaining quality as you scale? 19 7 Comments Farhad Alessandro Mohammadi Mamazen • 18K followers Alignment Isn’t a Buzzword, It’s a Red-Flag Detector. Studios that “get their money back first” poison every cap-table downstream. - 70/30 equity split (founders > studio) keeps talent motivated - Dual Entity structure separates BuildCo burn from FundCo returns—so nobody cashes in before investors do. Do a quick sanity check: if EBITDA or early exits for the studio are baked in before Series A, you just found your red flag. 13 Daril Fannin KINO • 5K followers 👥Crowdfunding vs. Crowd Investing💰: A lot of you disagreed with my post on crowdfunding. But maybe there’s a better way to fund feature films: crowd INVESTING. Crowdfunding is a viable option if you’re looking to finance a low budget web series. But it’s far from a reliable or scalable method, especially when you need $500,000 or more for a feature film. This is where crowd investing comes in. Platforms like Republic allow filmmakers to raise larger sums of money by offering a share of profits in exchange for investments. Unlike crowdfunding, crowd investing turns supporters into investors who are betting on your film’s success. Generally, crowd investing raises more capital than crowdfunding, it bakes in an audience (aka: they’re financially motivated to help promote the film when its released), it’s easier than traditional financing, and it keeps the ownership with the filmmakers. While this model can be complex, it’s the right choice if you’re looking for a more sustainable funding strategy. Note: I’m still of the STRONG opinion that this shouldn’t be your entire film’s budget, but a small percentage of capital raised (last in, first out) to help de-risk the investment by engaging the audience! #CrowdInvesting #FilmFinance 44 19 Comments John Roman BattlBox • 11K followers Everyone wants the freedom of bootstrapping. No one talks about the pressure. The day before Commerce Roundtable, we sat down in Miami for one of the realest conversations we've had on ASOM Pod. No investors. No runway. Just the reality of what it takes to build from scratch. With Rytis Lauris, Co-Founder and CEO of Omnisend, joining us, we dug into: - How customer-funded growth forces you to stay sharp - Why transparency builds loyalty faster than perks ever could - What happens when lean teams embrace constraint instead of fighting it - Why bootstrapping is not a strategy, it's a mindset If you're building with limited resources and unlimited ambition, this one is for you. 31 15 Comments Drew F. Every week, I see new launches backed by big names. The traction looks solid. The first revenue wave comes fast. But here’s the uncomfortable truth that MRR and ARR both have an R. Recurring. And that’s where most creator-led businesses start to collapse. Distribution gives you the first bump. Retention comes only if the product is strong. Too many businesses are mistaking distribution for product-market fit. If you’re a creator thinking of building, remember this: the world already knows you can drive eyeballs. What they don’t know is whether your product can stand on its own once the novelty wears off. That’s the real test. And that’s what makes a business, not just a launch. 40 12 Comments Show more posts Show fewer posts Explore top content on LinkedIn Find curated posts and insights for relevant topics all in one place.
